items.title: Joel Dorn interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2007
items.q: My biggest influences as producers, I mean I love what Nesuhi did, I love what John Hammond did, I love what Alfred Lion did and Orrin Keepnews and you know, Norman Granz, all the great jazz producers.

ctx.x: When you said I’ve got some new ideas, you take an artist who’s already established or semi-established, what kind of ideas would you present to that artist?

Well I’ll give you a couple of real examples but when I say I had new ideas like everybody who wants to be a record producer says well here’s how I would record this person and that person. Jazz is not the only music I like, I’m not a jazz producer. I have worked with a lot of jazz artists. I’m a record producer. One of the things I got criticized for, and one of the things that made me successful on those Atlantic years, the same thing, was I took people like Rahsaan and Yusef and Les McCann and Eddie Harris — I…
Let me drop the needle for you. Okay?
